title: Write product spec and content guide
prompt: Read ../planning/03_content_blueprint.md, ../planning/02_decisions.md (D1-D44) and skim ../planning/00_context_brief.md. Write two public-safe docs for this repo. (1) docs/SPEC.md: the complete product spec a developer needs: core idea, cast and Ara's voice, module template, all 10 modules (title, topic, learning objectives, lesson card outline of 6-8 cards each, module game with mechanic, loop, scoring and win/lose rules, badge name), the 6 arcade games (same detail, plus first-run 60-second Ara briefing script outline), Fact or Fake spec (item schema, sets practice/form_A/form_B, d-prime and c scoring, Truth Radar), Daily Challenge (date-seeded, rotates the 11 endless games + 3 practice items, Wordle-style emoji share text), Library (Myths, Diksyunaryo, Komiks Season 1 with 10 episodes, one unlocked per module), rewards (XP values, badges, streak with one freeze per week, printable certificate after all 10 modules generated client-side with typed name not stored), Me screen and the 5 accessibility settings, Report button (mailto AIKasalig@gmail.com, prefilled subject [ARAW] Report: <category>, screen, item id, app version, device), navigation per breakpoint, screen list. (2) docs/CONTENT_GUIDE.md: tone, Ara voice lines style, health-accuracy rules and a 'safe facts' list (well-established facts we may use: dengue warning signs, no herbal dengue cure, antibiotics vs viruses, do not stop maintenance meds without a doctor, FDA product verification, vaccine safety monitoring framed blame-free, etc.), villain cards (Dr. Fake, Miracle Mike, Fear Monger, Conspiracy Kuya, Kwento Kim), fictional naming rules, review_status, FAKE stamp rule. EXCLUDE internal project details: no Form 2/Form 5 references, no pilot LGU names, partners, budgets, staff, targets or funding numbers (credit line 'An AIKasalig project · DOST-PCHRD · National University' is allowed). Also create docs/DECISIONS-LOG.md with a header. No code in this task. Commit with message 'T00: product spec and content guide'.

title: Scaffold app, tooling, tokens and responsive shell
prompt: Create the project by hand (no interactive generators): package.json with scripts dev, build (tsc --noEmit && vite build), preview, test (vitest run --reporter=dot), e2e (playwright test --reporter=line), verify (npm run build && npm run test && npm run e2e). Install deps per CLAUDE.md stack and run 'npx playwright install chromium'. Configure vite (base './', preact preset), tsconfig strict, vitest (jsdom), playwright with projects phone 360x740 isMobile hasTouch, tablet 820x1180, desktop 1440x900, webServer = vite preview on a fixed port. Build src/styles/tokens.css + base.css from CLAUDE.md tokens and self-hosted fonts. Build the app shell: hash router, responsive navigation (bottom tabs <600, tablet layout 600-1023, side nav >=1024), header with XP and streak chips and a Report flag button on every screen, beta disclaimer footer/banner, placeholder screens Home/Learn/Arcade/Library/Me/Report, store module (versioned localStorage with try/catch and in-memory fallback), settings module applying root classes, i18n.ts string catalog (en). Tests: unit tests for store and router; e2e smoke on all 3 projects: each tab reachable, correct nav per breakpoint, no horizontal overflow, axe has no serious violations. Make npm run verify pass, then commit.

title: Ara character, icons, sunrise splash and boot flow
prompt: Port Ara from design/mockup/Ara.dc.html into src/ui/Ara.tsx (SVG, props size and mood happy|wow|wink|sad|think, gentle idle bob that respects reduced motion, accessible label). Add an AraBubble component (speech bubble with tail, used everywhere). Port the 8-bit sunrise splash from design/mockup/Main.dc.html as the first-visit boot screen (pixel sunrise, ARAW wordmark in Press Start 2P, loading bar, SIMULAN button, credit line, beta note). Splash shows on first visit per session only and must not block screen readers (skip link). Make it responsive (scales crisp at all sizes, landscape too). Tests: unit for Ara props; e2e: splash shows then SIMULAN goes Home, on all 3 projects, no overflow. Verify, commit.

title: Home, Me, accessibility settings and Report screens
prompt: Build Home (design/mockup/Home.dc.html; desktop layout from DesktopHome.dc.html): Ara greeting by time of day with nickname, Continue card (next module, progress), Daily Challenge card (placeholder link for now), Arcade and Myth-of-the-day shortcuts, badge strip. Build Me (Me.dc.html): nickname input, inclusive avatar picker (6+ SVG avatars incl. lola, hijab, wheelchair user), stats, accessibility settings (5 toggles, all off by default, applied app-wide: larger text scales type ~1.15-1.25, high contrast theme, extra-large buttons, screen-reader hints adds extra aria descriptions, reduce motion), language row (English, more soon), About and licences (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 content). Build Report (Report.dc.html): categories, auto context (current screen, item id passed via query, app version from package.json, user agent summary), optional details, privacy note, mailto AIKasalig@gmail.com with encoded subject/body. Tests for settings effects, mailto building, avatars persisting; e2e all 3 projects incl. axe. Verify, commit.

title: Learn path and module runner engine
prompt: Build the Learn path (Learn.dc.html): 10 modules on a winding path on phone, wider path or grid on tablet/desktop, states done/current/locked, tap shows details sheet. Unlock rule: sequential. Build the content-driven module runner: types in src/modules/types.ts (Module, Card variants: info, reveal, choice (single correct + feedback), swipe-sort, poll, takeaway, story-hook), a runner screen (Lesson.dc.html look: close, progress bar, report flag with card id, Ara reacting), steps hook -> cards -> module game (lazy-loaded component slot) -> takeaway 'Kailan ako magtitiwala?' -> mini Fact or Fake round (5 practice items, slot) -> badge + XP + confetti -> unlocks next module and Komiks episode. Progress persists. Create stub content for m01 to test the engine. Tests: unit for unlock and XP logic and each card type; e2e complete a stub module on all 3 projects. Verify, commit.

title: Fact or Fake engine, scoring and Truth Radar
prompt: Build src/content/factOrFake/schema.ts (fields per docs/SPEC.md: id, format text|gc_screenshot|image|chatbot_answer, domain, truth, trick, difficulty, module, set practice|form_A|form_B, author, meta, text, image (SVG scene descriptor, synthetic), explanation, how_to_check, basis, review_status) and a validator. Build the game UI (FactOrFake.dc.html): realistic post renderers per format (Facebook-style post, Messenger GC bubble screenshot, sponsored ad with SVG synthetic image, chatbot answer), big FACT/FAKE buttons plus swipe gesture on touch, feedback card (why, how to check, trick chip, FAKE stamp on generated fakes), Report link with item id, end screen with XP and Truth Radar (accuracy meter + trusting/doubtful lean meter computed from d-prime and c with safe handling of 0/100% rates). Modes: module mini-round (5 practice items by module), free play (balanced random practice rounds of 10), and a hidden assessment mode for form_A/form_B (route only, not linked in UI). Seed 12 sample items for tests. Unit-test scoring math thoroughly. e2e all 3 projects. Verify, commit.

title: Write the full Fact or Fake item bank
prompt: Following docs/CONTENT_GUIDE.md, write the full item bank in src/content/factOrFake/items.ts: 20 form_A, 20 form_B (each 10 fact/10 fake, A and B matched item-for-item on domain, format, trick and difficulty), and at least 50 practice items spread across all 10 module topics (health misinformation, AI-in-health claims, AI-generated health content, scams, privacy, algorithms, chatbots, deepfakes, wellbeing, rights). Balanced fact/fake in every module slice. Facts must be well established; fakes must be plausible Filipino-context posts with a named trick. All fictional people/brands. review_status unreviewed. Replace the 12 seed items. Add tests that validate: schema, balance per set and per module, A/B matching, unique ids, no form items in practice selectors. Verify, commit.

title: Module 1 content + AI or Not? game
prompt: Write M1 'What Is AI, Really?' full content per docs/SPEC.md (hook, 6-8 cards with interactions, takeaway). Build the 'AI or Not?' swipe-sort game: everyday things (Facebook feed, face filter, calculator, rice-cooker timer, symptom-checker app, Maps traffic, spam filter, light switch, voice assistant, TV remote...) swiped into AI / Not AI with instant one-line explanations, 12 cards per round from a larger pool, score and XP, keyboard and button alternatives to swipe. Tests and e2e on all 3 projects. Verify, commit.

title: Module 2 content + Turuan si AI
prompt: Write M2 'How AI Learns and Makes Mistakes' content. Build 'Turuan si AI' (teach the misinfo detector): player labels ~10 English example posts as fake/real; a real tiny in-browser classifier (naive Bayes over word tokens) trains on them; test round shows it failing on Taglish and Cebuano fakes; a 'Why?' button highlights the words it relied on (explainability); player adds local-language examples and retrains; accuracy before/after shown in a simple bar. Unit-test the classifier deterministically. e2e all 3 projects. Verify, commit.

title: Module 3 content + Tanong kay Chatbot
prompt: Write M3 'AI and Your Health' content (port the 3 cards in design/mockup/Lesson.dc.html, extend to 7). Build 'Tanong kay Chatbot': Bea asks a chat assistant health questions; scripted answers; player rules each Tama / Mali / Magpatingin (see a health worker); red-flag symptom lessons; one privacy scenario (app asking for contacts, location, photos: choose permissions); 8 questions per round from a pool of 16+, feedback after each. Add a disabled 'Chatbot Sandbox (coming soon)' card explaining a local AI model is planned. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Module 4 content + Spot the Tactic
prompt: Write M4 'Tricks of Health Misinformation' content. Build 'Spot the Tactic': collectible villain cards (Dr. Fake, Miracle Mike, Fear Monger, Conspiracy Kuya, Kwento Kim) with SVG portraits in the ARAW style; posts appear and the player picks which trick is used (some posts are true: pick 'No trick, it is legit'); defeating a villain (3 correct in a row for that trick) unlocks its card and badge; card collection view. Then the module flows into a 10-item Fact or Fake practice round. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Module 5 content + Tita's GC
prompt: Write M5 'Check Before You Share' content (Pause, check who said it, look for another source; FDA verification, DOH, fact-checkers; replying kindly). Build 'Tita's GC': a branching mock Messenger family group chat (Lola Nena, Tita Baby, Kuya Jun the BHW, Bea, the player). Tita forwards a post; player picks reactions, verification steps and replies; replies scored on accuracy AND kindness; outcomes ripple (who believed it, who checked); at least 3 scenarios with 2+ branch points each and 3 endings each. Data-driven dialogue tree with a validator test (no dead ends). e2e all 3 projects. Verify, commit.

title: Opus review checkpoint 1
prompt: Review the app so far as a senior engineer, UX designer and health-content reviewer. Run npm run verify. Generate Playwright screenshots of every screen at the 3 viewports into build/screens-1/ (gitignored) and look at a representative sample. Check: visual fidelity to design/mockup, responsiveness and overflow, accessibility, Ara's voice, content accuracy and safety (no dosing/diagnosis, fictional names), code quality and test coverage, bundle size. Fix every critical or high issue directly yourself if small; write remaining issues as a prioritized checklist in build/REVIEW-1.md (commit it). Verify, commit.

title: Fix review 1 findings
prompt: Work through build/REVIEW-1.md top to bottom and fix every item you can, ticking each box as done (or noting why not). Keep tests green and add tests where the review found gaps. Verify, commit.

title: Arcade screen and shared game engine
prompt: Build src/games/engine: fixed-timestep loop, canvas sizing with letterbox + devicePixelRatio + resize/orientation handling, unified input (touch, mouse, keyboard), seeded RNG (mulberry32) with daily seed helper, sprite/shape drawing helpers in ARAW palette, pause on visibilitychange, a 'Pahinga muna!' break overlay after 10 minutes of play with a short recap, high scores in storage, standard GameShell UI (HUD, pause, how-to-play, game-over with Ara recap and XP, accessible text alternative descriptions of game state). First-run 60-second Ara briefing component (paged, skippable). Build the Arcade screen (Arcade.dc.html): featured daily game, 11 game tiles (6 arcade open, 5 module games unlock after M6-M10), details sheet, lazy-load each game. Include a tiny demo game used only by tests. Unit-test RNG determinism, loop timing, scaling math. e2e all 3 projects. Verify, commit.

title: Arcade game: Takbo, Data! (privacy)
prompt: Build Takbo, Data! per docs/SPEC.md on the engine: endless runner through a procedurally generated barangay (sari-sari store, jeepney, health center), Ara runs; pickups: safe freebies vs data-costing traps (name, birthday, PhilHealth number, ID photo, contacts); Privacy Shield meter drains on bad grabs and refills on safe pickups; tap/space to jump, swipe down to slide; speed ramps; seeded so the daily seed is reproducible; briefing script; end recap teaching 3 privacy tips. Unit tests for spawn rules and scoring; e2e plays a few seconds on all 3 projects. Verify, commit.

title: Arcade game: Feed Mo 'To (algorithms)
prompt: Build Feed Mo 'To: the player is the algorithm choosing which post to show Tita next from 3 candidates (generated from templates); Engagement meter vs Balanced-Feed meter; her feed visibly narrows into a bubble when chasing engagement; endless random users with different interests; game ends when either meter crashes; recap explains recommendation algorithms and filter bubbles and why scary health posts spread. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Arcade game: Luto ni Ara (prompting)
prompt: Build Luto ni Ara: kitchen time-management; customers order outputs (e.g. explain dengue to Lola in simple Tagalog, short); drag or tap prompt ingredients (role, audience, language, length, format, 'ask it to cite sources', 'say if unsure') into the pot before the timer ends; good prompts serve a good dish, missing ingredients serve funny wrong dishes with a one-line lesson; orders speed up and never repeat (seeded generator). Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Arcade game: Sino 'To? (voice-clone scams)
prompt: Build Sino 'To?: phone switchboard; incoming calls and voice notes shown as transcripts with caller cards (no audio in this phase); some are AI voice-clone scams (fake relative in hospital needing GCash, fake doctor, fake bank), some are genuine; player uses verification moves (ask the family secret question, call back the saved number, check with another relative, hang up) before choosing to help or refuse; scam scripts generated from templates; FAKE stamp on revealed scams; lives and streak. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Arcade game: Lamok Lamay (AI vision errors)
prompt: Build Lamok Lamay: water containers pop up (drawn on canvas); an 'AI camera' overlay draws boxes labelled larvae with confidence %; some boxes are false positives (seed, leaf bit) and some larvae are missed; player whacks real larvae and corrects the AI (tap a wrong box to reject, tap an unboxed larva to add); live precision and recall meters explained in plain words; speed ramps; recap ties to dengue prevention (cover, clean, drain water containers). Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Arcade game: Tawid, Lola! (automation bias)
prompt: Build Tawid, Lola!: Crossy-Road style lanes procedurally generated toward the health center; an AI navigation voice (text bubble) suggests GO or WAIT and is usually right but sometimes confidently wrong; Trust Meter rewards following it when correct and overriding when your own view disagrees; tap/arrow controls; seeded lanes; recap about over-relying on AI and keeping human judgment. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Module 6 content + Hati Tayo!
prompt: Write M6 'Katuwang si AI' (AI and jobs, AI as a tool) content. Build Hati Tayo!: task-splitting tycoon over endless days in Kuya Jun's BHW work or Aling Nena's sari-sari store; random tasks arrive (count stock, translate a leaflet, comfort a worried mother, decide on a referral, schedule visits); drag each to AI or Human; AI is fast on repetitive tasks but fails on empathy and judgment; day-end report; register as an arcade game after module completion. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Module 7 content + Gawa Ko 'To!
prompt: Write M7 'Gawa ni AI?' (generative AI, ownership, consent, labelling) content. Build Gawa Ko 'To!: a creative studio where the player assembles a barangay health-drive poster from random briefs using parts (AI-generated image, stock photo, neighbor's photo, slogan, artist illustration); points for labelling AI-made parts, asking consent before using a real person's face or voice, crediting artists; skipping steps leads to a 'reported' ending; the finished poster renders as SVG. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Module 8 content + Tulog na, Bea!
prompt: Write M8 'Pahinga Muna' (digital wellbeing, AI companions) content. Build Tulog na, Bea!: virtual-pet life sim; keep Bea's Sleep, Mood, Study and Social meters balanced across endless days; notifications, autoplay and an over-friendly AI companion pull her to the screen; player sets boundaries (focus mode, phone-free dinner, bedtime, mute group chats) with trade-offs; healthy-chatbot-use lesson. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Module 9 content + Sa Sapatos Nila
prompt: Write M9 'Para sa Lahat' (fairness and accessibility) content. Build Sa Sapatos Nila: a health-center AI kiosk; random users (Lola with blurry vision, Deaf teen, Ilocano-only farmer, wheelchair user, person without a smartphone) try to use it; the player plays through their eyes with simulated filters (blur, muted audio cues shown as missing captions, unfamiliar-language text, out-of-reach buttons) and then toggles fixes (voice, large text, language choice, captions, lower placement, assisted counter) until everyone is served; simulation filters must never break the app's own accessibility. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Module 10 content + OBJECTION!
prompt: Write M10 'Karapatan Mo' (rights and accountability: Data Privacy Act rights in plain words, right to be informed, to access, to object, to correct, to complain to the National Privacy Commission, right to a human review, who is responsible) content, kept general and accurate. Build OBJECTION!: Ace-Attorney-style barangay-hall hearing; cases generated from templates (health app leaked records, AI wrongly flagged a claim, clinic chatbot gave harmful advice); statements scroll; the player presses OBJECTION! on the false statement and presents the right evidence card or right; 3 strikes; case-closed summary. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Write Library content: myths, glossary, Komiks
prompt: Following docs/CONTENT_GUIDE.md write src/content/library/: myths.ts (at least 24 Philippine health myths: myth, fact, why people believe it, how to check, linked villain trick, related module), glossary.ts (about 32 plain-language AI terms: term, one-line meaning, funny Filipino example, module link), komiks.ts (Season 1 'The Miracle Tea', 10 episodes of 4-6 panels each, one per module topic, with the family cast and Ara, panel scene descriptors (setting, characters, expressions) plus dialogue, kind and non-shaming). All review_status unreviewed. Add validation tests. Verify, commit.

title: Library screens and Komiks reader
prompt: Build Library (Library.dc.html): segmented tabs Myths (flip cards, filter by topic, search), Diksyunaryo (search, alphabetical, cards), Komiks (episode list, locked until its module is done, reader with panels drawn as SVG scenes from the descriptors using the cast and Ara components, swipe/arrow navigation, accessible transcript). Myth-of-the-day on Home wired to real data. Responsive layouts for all sizes. Tests and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: Daily Challenge, streaks, badges and certificate
prompt: Build the Daily Challenge: date-seeded (Asia/Manila date), same for everyone that day: featured endless game run with the day's seed + 3 practice Fact or Fake items; Wordle-style result with emoji grid share text (copy to clipboard / Web Share API), one attempt per day. Streak with one freeze per week. Badge cabinet on Me (module badges, villain badges, Truth Radar balanced, streak badges). Certificate after all 10 modules: client-side printable page (print CSS) and PNG download from canvas, name typed and not stored, credit line. Tests (seed determinism, streak rules) and e2e. Verify, commit.

title: PWA, performance and responsive polish
prompt: Add PWA: manifest, icons generated from an SVG sun/Ara mark, service worker (vite-plugin-pwa allowed) caching the app shell and fonts for offline use after first visit. Performance: lazy-load all games/modules, check initial JS <= 200 KB gzip with a test script (add to verify), image/SVG weight check. Responsive polish: test every screen at 320, 360, 414, 768, 1024, 1440, 1920 widths and landscape phone; fix any overflow, cramped or stretched layouts, tap-target issues; ensure desktop/projector layout looks intentional. Add an e2e sweep across those widths. Verify, commit.

Fix critical/high issues directly if small; write the rest as a prioritized checklist in build/REVIEW-2.md. Verify, commit.
